contexts.text: The justification of self thence results.
Fatuous fire which comes forth from the justification of self.
They who have been purified from the loves of self and of the world, both within and without the Church, are justified by the Lord.
That they have been justified by the Lord. Signified.
That they have been purified and thus justified by the Lord. Signified.

Justification is not according to the common opinion, that all evils are wiped away... when they believe... (for) not the smallest evil a man has thought and done... is wiped away... But the case is this... Explained.
They who (are persuaded) that when they are justified there is no longer any evil with them...
Thus people believe that they are justified and saved...
Justified together () = when truth becomes good.
Still less do they believe that they are justified (by the truths and goods with them).
The Angels say... that evil and falsity are not... wiped away from them, and that they are not so justified...
It then appears as if... the man had been purified from evils; or, as they say, justified...
They who have confirmed themselves in the idea that they are justified, and thus devoid of sins... are remitted into the state of (their) evils...
(For example), that man is justified by faith alone...
Then... instead of justification they would acknowledge regeneration...
They who believe themselves... so far justified that they no longer have anything of evil, are... among the unjust; for they attribute good to themselves...
The reason they know so little about regeneration, is that they speak so much about... justification; and because they believe... that man is justified by faith alone...

In the other life, when they who have taken with them the opinion that man is justified in a moment by faith... apperceive that regeneration is effected by means indefinite in number... they are astounded...
How shall we be justified? () = that we are guilty. Explained.
They who justify () = those who are in good, and who lead to good. AC 9263:5.
Under Justice, see this reference. AC 9263:2.

Because I will not justify the wicked () = that such malignity is contrary to the Divine justice. To justify = to declare guiltless, and to acquit... (as) is evident from the judicial signification of this word, as also in Matthew: By thy words thou shalt be justified... (); and in Luke: Ye are they who justify yourselves before men... ().
These are they who justify themselves by this, - that they account all things of faith and love as a matter of merit...

Those who justify many = those who are wise; and in Heaven those are called wise who are in good; and those there are in good who commit Divine truths immediately to life... HH 348:2. AR 51:end. AE 72:2.
Preface. Summary concerning the Doctrines of the Roman Catholic Church, section V. The doctrinal things of the Roman Catholics concerning justification. Quoted. BE 4. BE 7.
Preface. Summary concerning the Doctrines of the Reformed Church, section III. The doctrinal things of the Reformed concerning justification by faith. Quoted. BE 9. BE 11.
(Conversation on the act of justification.)

That the Roman Catholics before the Reformation... held the very same doctrine of justification by faith in the merit of Christ, with the sole difference that they conjoined that faith with charity or good works. General article. BE 21.

That the universal Christian theology is at this day founded upon the idea of three gods, is manifestly evident from the doctrine of justification, which is the head of the doctrines of the Church with... both Roman Catholics and Protestants. This doctrine teaches that...
The mystery of justification opened.
Then saving justification will be given you.
To this I replied... that man by his own works and power should justify himself, but should still believe that not a grain of justification is from himself.
A council convoked [to consider] the justification of the elect by faith.
As in the present Church by the Holy Spirit is described the Divine operation, which is actual justification...

That the Divine virtue and operation which are meant by the Holy Spirit, are in general reformation and regeneration, and, according to these, renovation, vivification, sanctification, and justification... General article. TCR 149.
In the placing of merit in works lies hidden... the justification of self...
The faith of the present Church, which is said alone to justify...
A grey colour = justification from self.
They who justify themselves... reflect the rays of intellectual light, (like the colour white).
(The idea that men can be justified in a moment, refuted.)
On sudden justification. (By this doctrine many are led to believe that they can sin with impunity.)
As they did not understand what regeneration is, they invented justification... SE 5741.
Hence it may be evident what is meant by to be justified.
(Most people) do not know what is meant by justification; and therefore when they hear it preached about... they believe... that justification is to live before God...
Because they call themselves just or justified when they have faith; and by the justified they understand that they are not liable to condemnation for anything they think and will...
It is said that He shall justify these (), because to justify = to save, from Divine good; from which He is also called just.
The degrees of the progression of faith to good works, which they call the degrees of justification. Enumerated.
On justification and good works, from the Council of Trent.
(Conversation with Protestant priests concerning justification.)
The dogmas of the imputation of the merit of Christ, and of justification thereby, flowed forth from the idea of a Trinity of Persons...
